observations: The requested full-page <10s target has not passed. Both accepted new-tab full-page runs are complete, cache-free, about 14.8-14.9s.
A rolling 30-start/12s client budget deliberately makes request 31 no earlier than 12s. It is an empirical local protection policy, not a published upstream quota.
Rejected 8/200 and prior 8/100 both returned 429 on request 32; that observation does not establish an exact server window or unique limiting dimension.
The independent counts after 429 use each actual response timestamp, not the failed harness lateRequestCount default.
No cooldown was cleared, identity or IP rotated, credentials copied, automatic retry used, or source budget expanded.
Preconnection and HTTP preparation experiments are separately counted qualification only. Their earlier waiting is included; no shortcut is present in either accepted full-page benchmark.
HEAD returned 401 and OPTIONS returned 405; neither was adopted as a production preparation method. OPTIONS rejection permitted zero POST requests.
Resource Timing connect includes TLS. Client execution starts do not equal network send or upstream arrival; cold handshakes may bunch multiple sends.
RAF is a next-visible-frame approximation, not OS paint. Initial viewport targets are frozen before output insertion.
Upstream cache/load/network cannot be controlled; no universal optimum or continued availability is asserted.
